ex.s: SoFi Stadium is the go-to destination in the heart of Los Angeles for sports fans.
ex.t: SoFi体育场位于洛杉矶市中心，是体育迷们的首选目的地。

ex.s: Its calendar is always packed with headline-grabbing events.
ex.t: 它的活动日程总是排满了引人注目的重磅活动。

ex.s: A mile away, the H Hotel Los Angeles, with its stylish design, is ideal for a nice stay between events.
ex.t: 一英里外，洛杉矶H酒店以其时尚的设计，是赛事间隙惬意下榻的理想之选。

ex.s: For those seeking both comfort and convenience, the Renaissance Los Angeles Airport Hotel is just a short drive away.
ex.t: 对于既追求舒适又讲究便利的人，洛杉矶机场万丽酒店只需短途车程即可到达。

ex.s: If you enter through the wrong access point, you'll be turned around and redirected — so plan ahead.
ex.t: 如果你从错误的入口进入，会被拦下并重新指引——所以请提前规划。

ex.s: For those wishing to park near friends, all vehicles must have passes for the same zone and arrive together — spaces cannot be saved.
ex.t: 对于想把车停在朋友附近的人，所有车辆必须持有同一区域的停车证并同时到达——车位不能预留。

ex.s: Which hotel is nearest to the stadium?
ex.t: 哪家酒店离体育场最近？

ex.s: While going through the pages, he kept saying, wide-eyed: “How can there be this many words?” After a while, he looked at me and asked, “Do you know all these words, Mom?” I smiled, “I definitely do not know all these words,” I said.
ex.t: 翻页时，他睁大眼睛不停地说：“怎么会有这么多词？”过了一会儿，他看着我问：“妈妈，这些词你都认识吗？”我笑着说：“我肯定不是都认识。”

ex.s: “But that’s why this is one of my favorite books.”
ex.t: “但这正是它成为我最喜欢的书之一的原因。”

ex.s: I felt a small pain in my chest The dictionary was stolen at the end of my freshman year of college.
ex.t: 我感到胸口隐隐作痛。那本词典在我大学一年级结束时被偷了。

ex.s: “That’s so sad,” he said, “but you still know all those words, even without the book.” I realized that this was true.
ex.t: “那太遗憾了，”他说，“不过即使没有那本书，你依然认识那些词。”我意识到这话确实没错。

ex.s: Now I understand that although my son may be learning differently, he is still learning.
ex.t: 现在我明白，虽然儿子的学习方式可能不同，但他仍然在学习。

ex.s: It was given to Kevin as a gift.
ex.t: 它是作为礼物送给凯文的。

ex.s: It was a valuable limited edition.
ex.t: 那是珍贵的限量版。

ex.s: It is never too late to start.
ex.t: 什么时候开始都不算晚。

ex.s: Dictionaries are still a useful tool.
ex.t: 词典仍然是有用的工具。

ex.s: In line with longstanding initiatives to expand its green spaces, New York City is planting tens of thousands of trees each year.
ex.t: 为配合长期以来扩大绿色空间的举措，纽约市每年种植数万棵树木。

ex.s: The Parks Department is not oblivious to the issue.
ex.t: 公园管理局并非没有意识到这个问题。

ex.s: She said trees should not be viewed as the enemy.
ex.t: 她说，树木不应被视为敌人。

ex.s: “You have to think about what you would lose if you do that.” Oaks are keystone species, she pointed out, providing food and habitat for native insects, birds and other animals.
ex.t: “你得想想你那么做会失去什么。”她指出，橡树是关键物种，为本地的昆虫、鸟类和其他动物提供食物和栖息地。

ex.s: Participants were randomly divided into two groups: the “beauty” group was asked to actively consider and then rate the beauty of each object they viewed, while the control group just matched a line drawing of the object with the artwork itself.
ex.t: 参与者被随机分为两组：“美”组被要求主动思考并为所看到的每件物品的美打分，而对照组只是将物品的线描图与艺术品本身进行匹配。

ex.s: All participants were then tested on how they process information, and whether it's in a more practical or abstract way.
ex.t: 然后所有参与者都接受了测试，看他们如何处理信息，是以更实用还是更抽象的方式。

ex.s: While they were told the study was about cognitive processes, participants were asked about interests, with around half saying they had an artistic hobby.
ex.t: 虽然参与者被告知这项研究是关于认知过程的，但他们也被问及兴趣爱好，约一半人说自己有艺术爱好。

ex.s: Among those, the effect was greater: those with an artistic hobby in the beauty group scored over 25% higher on average for abstract thinking than those with an artistic hobby in the control group.
ex.t: 在其中，效果更明显：有艺术爱好的“美”组在抽象思维上的平均得分比有艺术爱好的对照组高出25%以上。

ex.s: Emotional states of participants were also measured by asking about their feelings while completing the gallery task.
ex.t: 参与者的情绪状态也通过询问他们在完成画廊任务时的感受来衡量。

ex.s: Importantly, however, the beauty group did not report feeling any happier than the control group, suggesting that it was the engagement with beauty that influenced abstract thinking, rather than any overall positivity from the experience.
ex.t: 然而重要的是，美感组并没有报告比对照组更快乐，这表明影响抽象思维的是与美的接触，而不是这次经历带来的整体积极情绪。

ex.s: Admiring the beauty of art may be the ideal way to initiate the abstract cognitive processes.”
ex.t: 欣赏艺术之美或许是开启抽象认知过程的理想方式。”

ex.s: What was the beauty group asked to do with the clay objects?
ex.t: 美感组被要求对这些陶艺品做什么？

ex.s: Why were the participants’ emotional states measured?
ex.t: 为什么要测量参与者的情绪状态？

ex.s: What is the major finding of the study regarding the appreciation of art?
ex.t: 关于艺术欣赏，这项研究的主要发现是什么？

ex.s: Museums, once quiet places filled with history, are now full of digital excitement.
ex.t: 博物馆曾经是充满历史气息的安静场所，如今却处处洋溢着数字化的活力。

ex.s: AI can help identify the slightest signs of decay, such as cracks or discoloration, which are often invisible to the human eye. _____38_____ Moreover, by predicting future decay patterns, AI helps museums take preventive measures and improve preservation strategies.
ex.t: 人工智能可以帮助识别最轻微的损坏迹象，如裂纹或变色，这些往往肉眼难以察觉。____ 此外，通过预测未来的损坏趋势，人工智能帮助博物馆采取预防措施、改进保护策略。

ex.s: Museums are working together with AI ethicists to develop fair algorithms.
ex.t: 博物馆正与人工智能伦理学家合作，开发公平的算法。

ex.s: In short, AI is redefining the museum in all respects.
ex.t: 简而言之，人工智能正在从各个方面重新定义博物馆。

ex.s: Museums are not only places to store artworks, but also spaces for learning.
ex.t: 博物馆不仅是存放艺术品的场所，也是学习的空间。

ex.s: Furthermore, AI-powered virtual guides are replacing traditional tour guides.
ex.t: 此外，由人工智能驱动的虚拟导览正在取代传统导游。

ex.s: Sure, my friends and I loved to _____46_____ about how bored we were in the middle of nowhere; _____47_____ , as I finish up my junior year of college, I’m convinced that it took _____48_____ our small town to realize how much we actually loved it and what exactly we loved about it.
ex.t: 当然，我和朋友们喜欢____46____我们在偏僻之地有多无聊；____47____，当我念完大三，我确信正是____48____我们的小镇，才让我意识到我们有多爱它、以及我们到底爱它什么。

ex.t: 那里的生活节奏缓慢，人们____彼此之间的联系。

ex.t: 我感激成长过程中所拥有的____，也知道无论下一段冒险把我带向何方，我都能____自己的小镇根基引领我走向正确的方向。

ex.s: It is also common for them _____56_____ (hold) during traditional Chinese holidays such as the Spring Festival and the Mid-Autumn Festival, as well as other local festivals.
ex.t: 它们也常在春节、中秋节等中国传统节日以及其他地方性节日期间____（举行）。

ex.s: In addition to being venues for buying and selling, daji are occasions for socializing and entertainment.
ex.t: 除了作为买卖场所，大集也是社交和娱乐的场合。

ex.s: As the snow came down more and more heavily, Emily was directed off the highway.
ex.t: 雪越下越大，Emily被引导驶离了高速公路。

ex.s: While Emily was driving on a narrow stretch of road, her car slid into a ditch (沟).
ex.t: 当Emily在一段狭窄的道路上行驶时，她的车滑进了沟里。

ex.s: When Emily rolled down the window, Rachel asked if she was okay and told her it was not safe to stay overnight in the car.
ex.t: 当Emily摇下车窗时，Rachel问她是否还好，并告诉她整夜待在车里不安全。

ex.s: In the cafe, the couple bought Emily a hot chocolate and listened patiently as she explained her desperate situation: she was about a hundred miles from her destination, her car was completely stuck, and her entire holiday plan could be ruined.
ex.t: 在咖啡馆里，这对夫妇给Emily买了一杯热巧克力，耐心地听她讲述自己的困境：她离目的地还有约一百英里，车彻底陷住了，整个假期计划都可能泡汤。

ex.s: The D.C. area is home to many outstanding Chinese restaurants, but diners willing to travel outside the city limits will also be rewarded.
ex.t: 华盛顿特区有许多出色的中餐馆，但愿意走出市区就餐的食客也会有所收获。

ex.s: This not-so-hidden-anymore fine restaurant for Sichuan cuisine is inside the Days Inn off New York Avenue.
ex.t: 这家已不再那么隐秘的川菜精品餐厅位于纽约大道旁的戴斯酒店内。

ex.s: Dandan noodles and mapo tofu are sure bets.
ex.t: 担担面和麻婆豆腐是绝对不会踩雷的选择。

ex.s: Panda Gourmet offers online ordering for takeout, and delivery is now an option.
ex.t: Panda Gourmet提供外卖在线点餐，现在也支持配送。

ex.s: Open from 11:00 am to 9:45 pm Closed on Tuesday.
ex.t: 营业时间：上午11:00至晚上9:45，周二休息。

ex.s: The spacious dining room is regularly filled with customers enjoying dumplings and a variety of noodle and rice dishes.
ex.t: 宽敞的餐厅里经常坐满享用饺子以及各种面食和米饭菜肴的顾客。

ex.s: What service is available only at Panda Gourmet?
ex.t: 哪项服务只有Panda Gourmet提供？

ex.s: It is open only on weekdays.
ex.t: 它只在工作日营业。

ex.s: Roland Reisley turned 101 years old in May and is in remarkable health.
ex.t: Roland Reisley今年5月满101岁，身体状况非常好。

ex.s: “I am the last original client of Frank Lloyd Wright, still living in the home he designed for me,” Reisley said, sitting in the bright open living room of the home designed by the famous architect.
ex.t: “我是弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特最后一位健在的原始客户，至今仍住在他为我设计的房子里，”Reisley坐在由这位著名建筑师设计的明亮通透的客厅里说道。

ex.s: Back in 1951, Reisley was just 26, newly married and ready to put down roots.
ex.t: 早在1951年，Reisley只有26岁，新婚不久，准备安家扎根。

ex.s: On their first trip out, they were greeted with such enthusiasm from the 10 families who’d already established homes there that they decided to join.
ex.t: 第一次实地探访时，已在那里安家的10户人家热情相迎，这让他们决定加入。

ex.s: It is made with local materials, has a flat roof, wood paneling, concrete floors and custom-made furniture.
ex.t: 它使用当地材料建造，有平屋顶、木镶板、混凝土地面和定制家具。

ex.s: The house is now listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
ex.t: 这座房子如今已被列入《国家史迹名录》。

ex.s: Reisley believes that his devotion to the home and the community are what have kept him in such good health all of these years.
ex.t: Reisley相信，正是对这座房子和这片社区的热爱，让他多年来一直保持着如此好的健康状态。

ex.s: It is older than its owner.
ex.t: 它比主人年纪还大。

ex.s: It is put up for sale.
ex.t: 它被挂牌出售。

ex.s: What can be inferred about Reisley from the last paragraph?
ex.t: 从最后一段能推断出关于雷伊斯利的什么？

ex.s: He is very attached to Wright buildings.
ex.t: 他非常钟爱赖特的建筑。

ex.s: He is devoted to health education.
ex.t: 他致力于健康教育。

ex.s: He is an expert in home decoration.
ex.t: 他是家居装饰方面的专家。

ex.s: He is passionate about tourism.
ex.t: 他对旅游业充满热情。

ex.s: Simple readings are now readily available on our phones and wearables.
ex.t: 如今，我们的手机和可穿戴设备都能轻松给出这些简单读数。

ex.s: But elevation is necessarily relative: only the choice of a reference point allows us to express numerically the height of an object or a location.
ex.t: 但海拔高度必然是相对的：只有选择一个参照点，我们才能用数值表示物体或地点的高度。

ex.s: The idea of sea level as a reference point for elevations has by now been around for so long as to go essentially unnoticed-we mention it without even considering what it means.
ex.t: 以海平面作为海拔参照点的想法如今已存在如此之久，以至于几乎被人忽视——我们提到它时甚至不去思考它的含义。

ex.s: That the concept has a history is easily ignored.
ex.t: 这个概念有其历史，这一点很容易被忽视。

ex.s: We tend to forget that sea level is a product of technically and culturally determined assumptions.
ex.t: 我们往往忘记，海平面是技术性和文化性预设共同的产物。

ex.s: This is how I began my search for the conceptual history of sea level.
ex.t: 我就是这样开始探寻海平面的概念史的。

ex.s: Some mountains are getting higher.
ex.t: 一些山正在变高。

ex.s: Data on wearables are misleading.
ex.t: 可穿戴设备上的数据有误导性。

ex.s: The concept of elevation is relative.
ex.t: 海拔的概念是相对的。

ex.s: The reference point is hard to locate.
ex.t: 参照点难以确定。

ex.t: 第3段主要讲什么？

ex.s: How the altimeter was invented.
ex.t: 高度计是如何发明的。

ex.t: 文中提到的那本书可以取什么书名？

ex.s: Little do they know that as they do so, a burst of energy is sent up to street level to help charge an electric car.
ex.t: 他们几乎不知道，在这么做的同时，一股能量被传送到街道层面，用来给一辆电动汽车充电。

ex.s: “I am pleasantly surprised, because I am always looking for where to plug it in,” Espinoza said before catching the subway in a working-class area of southern Barcelona.
ex.t: “我感到惊喜，因为我一直在找哪里能给车充电，”Espinoza在南巴塞罗那一个工人阶层社区赶地铁前说道。

ex.s: “And if it is from energy from the trains’ brakes, then even better.”
ex.t: “如果用的是列车刹车产生的能量，那就更好了。”

ex.s: Regenerative brakes have been in trains for decades and are also used in some cars.
ex.t: 再生制动技术在列车中已应用了几十年，一些汽车也在使用。

ex.s: They consist of an electric motor which collects energy used in the braking action that would be lost as heat by conventional brakes.
ex.t: 它们由一个电动机构成，该电机收集制动过程中原本会被传统刹车以热量形式耗散的能量。

ex.s: Alvaro Luna, a professor of electrical engineering, said that the system is innovative in so far as it allows for recycled energy to be redirected to specific local uses — in this case powering electric cars parked nearby.
ex.t: 电气工程教授Alvaro Luna表示，该系统的创新之处在于它能让回收的能量转向特定的本地用途——在这里就是为停在附近的电动汽车供电。

ex.s: What is Espinoza’s concern?
ex.t: Espinoza关心的是什么？

ex.t: 第五段讨论了再生制动的哪个方面？

ex.s: If only the effort they put into avoiding responsibility could be redirected into, well, actual responsibility.
ex.t: 要是他们用来逃避责任的那份力气能转移到——嗯——真正的责任上就好了。

ex.s: Here are four simple and practical ways.
ex.t: 这里有四个简单实用的方法。

ex.s: Teaching kids work ethic is to gently and consistently push them toward responsibility, determination, and pride in their efforts. ____40____ No worry.
ex.t: 培养孩子的敬业精神，就是温和而持续地把他们推向责任感、毅力和对自己努力的自豪。____ 别担心。

ex.s: The key is consistency.
ex.t: 关键在于持之以恒。

ex.s: Sometimes, a cleaner living room is the best reward.
ex.t: 有时候，更整洁的客厅就是最好的奖励。

ex.s: Progress can be slow, and you’ll wonder if it’s all sinking in.
ex.t: 进步可能很慢，你会怀疑这一切是否真的被他们吸收了。

ex.s: Not every child is born with the willpower of a marathon runner.
ex.t: 并非每个孩子都生来就有马拉松选手那样的意志力。

ex.s: I never thought I could be a writer.
ex.t: 我从没想过自己能成为一名作家。

ex.s: I was teaching poetry, encouraging students to write about their ____45____.
ex.t: 我当时教诗歌，鼓励学生写他们的____45____。

ex.s: And then, at the end of the lesson, one child asked me a question: “Have you always wanted to be a ____46____, Miss?” I explained that when I was his age, I actually wanted to be a writer, but I didn’t think I quite had what it ____47____.
ex.t: 然后，在课程结束时，一个孩子问我一个问题：“老师，您一直想当一名____46____吗？”我解释说，我在他这个年纪时其实想当作家，但我觉得自己并不具备所需的____47____。

ex.s: The boy replied with a ____48____ look, “Well, you are telling us to live our dreams when you haven’t even done it yourself.
ex.t: 男孩带着____48____的神情回答：“可是，你自己在都还没做到的情况下，却叫我们去追逐梦想。”

ex.s: I was struck speechless — he was ____50____.
ex.t: 我被问得哑口无言——他是____。

ex.s: Who was I to ____51____ them on bravery and risk when I had never taken myself for my own ____52____ seriously?
ex.t: 我从未认真对待过自己的____，又有什么资格____他们去勇敢和冒险呢？

ex.s: There were times when I found myself wondering if I should pack it all in, but the boy’s words kept ringing in my ears: I knew I needed nothing else to succeed but a bit of ____54____ and hard work.
ex.t: 曾有段时间我怀疑自己是否该放弃，但男孩的话一直在我耳边回响：我知道要成功，除了一点____54____和努力，我别无所需。

ex.s: Angela, a tai chi ____57____ (instruct) with twenty-eight years of experience, says that a successful hour of tai chi is an hour with no negative thoughts.
ex.t: 有28年经验的太极____57____（教练）Angela说，成功的一小时太极就是没有负面想法的一小时。

ex.s: Although not a morning person, I begin my lesson with Angela and about twenty others at a Sydney community centre courtyard at 7 am.
ex.t: 虽然不是早起的人，我还是在早上7点和安吉拉以及另外约二十人在悉尼一个社区中心的院子里开始上课。

ex.s: In tai chi, the dan tian is your qi core and qi in Chinese means life force.
ex.t: 在太极拳中，丹田是你的气之核心，而“气”在中文里意为生命力。

ex.t: 接着我们练习太极招式，Angela所教的这一流派共有____四十二式。

ex.t: 今天我们只练前九式。

ex.t: 课程结束时，尽管才早上8点、仍然____（是）很早，我却感觉神清气爽。

ex.s: As far as I can remember, I’ve always been a night owl.
ex.t: 据我所记，我一直是个夜猫子。

ex.s: I woke up at 6am.
ex.t: 我早上6点醒来。

ex.s: “You’re 20, but your heart is 40!” he said.
ex.t: “你20岁，但你的心脏已经40岁了！”他说。

ex.s: The City of Burlington public art program is presenting a series of temporary public art signs at the Beachway in conjunction with the Ontario Culture Days.
ex.t: Burlington市公共艺术项目正与安大略文化节合作，在Beachway展出一系列临时公共艺术标识。

ex.s: This project will select 10 visual artists and 10 writers to create artwork that will be displayed on temporary signs along the multi-use path.

ex.s: Often students come to the classroom believing that learning can’t be fun and that what they learn isn’t relevant to the real world — much less to their personal interests.
ex.t: 学生们常常带着这样的看法走进教室：学习不可能有趣，所学内容与现实世界无关——更谈不上与他们的个人兴趣有关。

ex.s: I’ve discovered that if I show students how what they learn is relevant to my hobbies, they’re much more willing to make connections to their personal interests and develop their own hobbies.
ex.t: 我发现，如果我向学生展示所学内容与我的爱好的关联，他们就更愿意把知识与自己的兴趣联系起来，并培养出自己的爱好。

ex.s: When I first brought my hobbies to my classroom, I was focused on how doing so would build engagement and help my students understand concepts in science.
ex.t: 最初把爱好带进课堂时，我关注的是这样做能如何提高参与度、帮助学生理解科学概念。

ex.s: When I let them see an aspect of my life outside of school, some students who were also interested in cars connected with me more and became more engaged in my courses.
ex.t: 当我让他们看到我校外生活的一面时，一些同样对汽车感兴趣的学生与我更有共鸣，也更投入我的课程。

ex.s: What started as an experiment is now more of a philosophy.
ex.t: 起初只是一次实验，如今更像一种理念。

ex.s: Best of all, my passion for my hobbies seems to inspire them to be passionate about finding their own.

ex.s: After we had twins and became a family of five, my husband and I decided to move from London back to Yorkshire, to be closer to my parents.
ex.t: 在有了双胞胎、成为五口之家后，我和丈夫决定从伦敦搬回约克郡，离我父母更近一些。

ex.s: We moved them in with us until the build was complete.
ex.t: 打包父母房子的感觉就像是一场盛大的告别——那个房间、那些回忆、我在那里总能感受到的安全感和庇护感。

ex.t: 一片沉默，爸爸继续喝着茶，我屏住了呼吸。

ex.s: I breathed a huge sigh of relief: I had expected sadness, maybe even doubt, but Dad was already looking to the future.
ex.t: 我长长地松了一口气：我本以为会是伤感，甚至可能是疑虑，但爸爸已经在展望未来。

ex.s: Yes, it was a huge goodbye in so many ways, but it was also the start of something new — an adventure in multigenerational living.
ex.t: 是的，从很多方面说这是一次巨大的告别，但它也是新事物的开端——一场多代同堂生活的冒险。

ex.s: Hearing Dad’s cheerfulness, I realised that what I’d been seeing as “the end of an era” was actually the start of a new one.
ex.t: 听到爸爸的乐观，我意识到我眼中的“一个时代的终结”其实是一个新时代的开始。

ex.s: Similarly, the corporate world has certainly known its fair share of disruption, yet it is only in the last couple of decades that the “Disruptor” has become a recognisable figure in the way we talk about big business.
ex.t: 类似地，企业界当然也经历过不少颠覆，但“颠覆者”成为我们谈论大企业时一个可辨识的角色，不过是近几十年的事。

ex.t: 在早期，颠覆者会被称作创新者。

ex.s: Yet while an Innovator creates something new, the Disruptor is defined as much by what they destroy as by what they create.
ex.t: 然而，创新者创造新事物，而颠覆者的定义，既在于他们创造了什么，也在于他们摧毁了什么。

ex.s: The Disruptor forces change; the clean-up is somebody else’s problem.
ex.t: 这种态度最好概括为"快速行动，打破常规"。

ex.s: Imagine there is a fence along a road.
ex.t: 想象路边有一道栅栏。

ex.t: 对我们现在来说，这道栅栏似乎只不过是个障碍。

ex.s: When faced with such a fence, Chesterton thinks the fact that we can’t see the point of the fence is why we should not tear it down.
ex.t: 面对这样的栅栏，Chesterton认为，正因为我们看不出它的意义，才更不应该拆掉它。

ex.s: If you think you can do without the fence because you’ve never seen a fox, consider if the existence of the fence is precisely why you’ve never seen one.

ex.s: Importantly, Chesterton is not saying that things can never be reformed.

ex.s: His is a preventive principle rather than an outright prohibition.

ex.s: Is comprehension the same whether a person reads a text onscreen or on paper?
ex.t: 一个人在屏幕上读和在纸上读，理解力是一样的吗？

ex.s: And are listening to and viewing content as effective as reading the written word when covering the same material?

ex.s: The answers to both questions are often “no”.
ex.t: 这两个问题的答案往往是否定的。

ex.s: When reading texts of several hundred words or more, learning is generally more successful when it’s on paper than onscreen.
ex.t: 阅读几百词或更长的文本时，在纸上学习通常比在屏幕上更成功。

ex.s: The differences between print and digital reading results are partly related to paper’s physical properties.
ex.t: 纸质阅读与电子阅读效果之间的差异，部分与纸张的物理特性有关。

ex.s: With paper, there is a literal laying on of hands, along with the visual geography of distinct pages.
ex.t: 对于纸质书，是真的用手去翻阅，再加上不同页面的视觉布局。

ex.s: People often link their memory of what they’ve read to how far into the book it was or where it was on the page.
ex.t: 人们常把对所读内容的记忆与它出现在书中的位置或页面上的位置联系起来。

ex.s: According to this theory, people approach digital texts with a mindset suited to social media, which are often not so serious, and devote less mental effort than when they are reading print.
ex.t: 根据这一理论，人们以适合社交媒体的心态来对待数字文本（社交媒体往往没那么严肃），因此投入的心思比读纸质书时少。

ex.s: However, for maximizing learning where mental focus and reflection are called for, educators shouldn’t assume all media are the same, even when they contain identical words.
ex.t: 然而，在需要专注与思考、追求学习效果最大化时，教育者不应认为所有媒介都是一样的，即使它们包含相同的文字。

ex.s: So, if we accept that the universe is unknowable, we also accept we will never know if we live in a computer simulation.

ex.s: And then, we can shift our inquiry from “Is the universe a computer simulation? ” to “Can we model the universe as a computer simulation? ” Modelling reality is what we do.
ex.t: 然后，我们可以将我们的探究从"宇宙是一个计算机模拟吗？"转移到"我们能否将宇宙建模为一个计算机模拟？"建模现实正是我们所做的事。

ex.s: Now that we are in the information age, we have new concepts such as the computer, information processing, virtual reality, and simulation.
ex.t: 既然我们处于信息时代，我们就有了计算机、信息处理、虚拟现实和模拟等新概念。

ex.s: Models are not the reality, however.
ex.t: 但模型不是现实。

ex.s: There is no point in arguing if the universe is a clock, a set of particles or an output of computation.
ex.t: 争论宇宙是一座钟、一组粒子还是计算的输出，是毫无意义的。

ex.s: All these models are tools to deal with the unknown and to make discoveries.
ex.t: 所有这些模型都是应对未知和做出发现的工具。

ex.s: It can be imagined that comparable to the process of building previous scientific models, developing the “computer simulation” metaphor-based model will also be a hugely rewarding exercise.
ex.t: 可以想象，与构建以往科学模型的过程类似，发展这种基于"计算机模拟"隐喻的模型也将是一项极具价值的实践。

ex.s: The experiment of estimation he conducted showed that in some cases, the average of a large number of independent estimates could be quite accurate.

ex.s: When enough of these errors are averaged together, they cancel each other out, resulting in a more accurate estimate.

ex.s: If people are similar and tend to make the same errors, then their errors won’t cancel each other out.

ex.s: In more technical terms, the wisdom of crowds requires that people’s estimates be independent.

ex.s: For instance, the average obtained from the estimates of four discussion groups of five was significantly more accurate than the average obtained from 20 independent individuals.

ex.t: 哈拉米略的学生居住的社区里，新鲜食物和绿地很难找到，快餐店的数量超过了杂货店。

ex.t: “他们来找我们时，认为蔬菜很讨厌，泥土很讨厌，昆虫很讨厌。”虽然有些人一开始害怕昆虫、厌恶泥土，但大多数人都渴望尝试新事物。

ex.s: Reading Art: Art for Book Lovers is a celebration of an everyday object — the book, represented here in almost three hundred artworks from museums around the world.
ex.t: 《阅读艺术：书迷的艺术》是对一件日常物品——书——的礼赞，书中收录了来自世界各地博物馆的近三百件艺术作品。

ex.s: The image of the reader appears throughout history, in art made long before books as we now know them came into being.
ex.t: 读者的形象贯穿整个历史，出现在远早于我们今天所熟知的书籍诞生之前的艺术作品中。

ex.s: In this “book of books,” artworks are selected and arranged in a way that emphasizes these connections between different eras and cultures.
ex.t: 在这本"书中的书"中，艺术作品的选取和编排方式强调了不同时代和文化之间的联系。

ex.s: These scenes may have been painted hundreds of years ago, but they record moments we can all relate to.
ex.t: 这些场景也许是数百年前画下的，但它们记录了我们每个人都能感同身受的时刻。

ex.s: Before the wide use of the printing press, books were treasured objects and could be works of art in their own right.
ex.t: 在印刷术广泛使用之前，书籍是珍贵的物品，其本身就可以是艺术品。

ex.s: Continued developments in communication technologies were once believed to make the printed page outdated.
ex.t: 通信技术的不断发展曾让人们以为印刷书页将会过时。

ex.s: From a 21st-century point of view, the printed book is certainly ancient, but it remains as interactive as any battery-powered e-reader.
ex.t: 从21世纪的角度看，印刷书固然古老，但它仍像任何电池供电的电子阅读器一样具有互动性。

ex.s: To serve its function, a book must be activated by a user: the cover opened, the pages parted, the contents reviewed, perhaps notes written down or words underlined.
ex.t: 要发挥其功能，书必须由使用者来"激活"：打开封面，翻动书页，浏览内容，也许写下笔记或划出重点。

ex.s: And in contrast to our increasingly networked lives where the information we consume is monitored and tracked, a printed book still offers the chance of a wholly private, “off-line” activity.
ex.t: 与我们日益网络化的生活——我们所消费的信息被监控和追踪——形成对比的是，印刷书仍提供一种完全私密、"离线"活动的机会。

ex.s: The printed book is not totally out of date.

ex.s: As cities balloon with growth, access to nature for people living in urban areas is becoming harder to find.
ex.t: 随着城市不断膨胀扩张，生活在城市地区的人们越来越难接触到大自然。

ex.s: If you’re lucky, there might be a pocket park near where you live, but it’s unusual to find places in a city that are relatively wild.
ex.t: 如果幸运，你住的地方附近可能有一个袖珍公园，但在城市里找到相对野生的地方是不寻常的。

ex.s: For example, one participant’s experience of “We sat and listened to the waves at the beach for a while” was assigned the categories “sitting at beach” and “listening to waves.”
ex.t: 例如，一位参与者"我们坐在海滩上听了一会儿海浪"的体验被归入"坐在海滩"和"听海浪"两类。

ex.s: For example, the experience of walking along the edge of water might be satisfying for a young professional on a weekend hike in the park.
ex.t: 例如，沿水边行走的体验可能让一位在公园周末徒步的年轻职场人士感到满足。

ex.s: Pocket parks are now popular.
ex.t: 口袋公园现在很流行。

ex.t: 城市中很难找到自然野趣。

ex.s: Walking is the best way to gain access to nature.

ex.t: 不过，我确实记得作为一个彻头彻尾的初学者是什么感觉。

ex.s: Serving hard-to-find Thai dishes in an elegant atmosphere, the restaurant is true to Thai cuisine’s roots, yet still manages to add a special twist.
ex.t: 餐厅在优雅的氛围中供应难觅的泰式菜肴，既忠于泰菜的本源，又巧妙增添了特别的变化。

ex.s: With millions of people likely to take on DIY projects over that coming weeks, new research shows that more than half of people are planning to make the most of the long, warm summer days to get jobs done.
ex.t: 数以百万计的人可能在接下来的几周里动手做DIY项目，新的研究显示，超过一半的人打算利用漫长而温暖的夏日把活干完。

ex.s: The average spend per project will be around £ 823.
ex.t: 每个项目的平均花费约为823英镑。

ex.s: Though DIY has traditionally been seen as male hobby, the research shows it is women now leading the charge.
ex.t: 尽管DIY传统上被视为男性的爱好，但研究显示，如今是女性冲在最前面。

ex.s: I was about 13 when an uncle gave me a copy of Jostein Gaarder’s Sophie’s World.
ex.t: 我大约13岁时，一位叔叔送了我一本乔斯坦·贾德写的《苏菲的世界》。

ex.s: It was full of ideas that were new to me so I spent the summer with my head in and out of that book.
ex.t: 书里满是对我来说全新的思想，所以我整个夏天都沉浸在那本书里，时而读时而想。

ex.s: It is not an explanation, but an invitation to think and experience philosophy.
ex.t: 它不是一种解释，而是对思考和体验哲学的邀请。

ex.s: The end result is a read in which we learn to wonder like Socrates, see like Thoreau, listen like Schopenhauer, and have no regrets like Nietzsche.
ex.t: 最终读到的，是我们学会像苏格拉底一样发问、像梭罗一样观察、像叔本华一样倾听、像尼采一样无怨无悔。

ex.s: This, more than a book about undestanding philosophy, is a book abour learning to use philosophy to improve a life.
ex.t: 这，与其说是一本关于理解哲学的书，不如说是一本关于学会用哲学改善生活的书。

ex.s: The Socrates Express is a fun, sharp book that draws readers in with its apparent simplicity and gradually pulls them in deeper thoughts on desire, loneliness, and aging.
ex.t: 《苏格拉底快线》是一本有趣而犀利的书，以其表面的简单吸引读者，逐渐将他们带入对欲望、孤独和衰老的更深思考。

ex.s: The invitation is clear: Weiner wants you to pick up a coffee or tea and sit down with this book.
ex.t: 邀请是明确的：韦纳想让你端起一杯咖啡或茶，坐下来读这本书。

ex.s: Its views on history are well-presented.

ex.s: Its ideas can be applied to daily life.

ex.s: Ask the tourists from around the world that flood into Yellowstone National Park what they most hope to see, and their answer is often the same: a grizzly bear.
ex.t: 问问涌入黄石国家公园的来自世界各地的游客他们最希望看到什么，答案往往相同：一只灰熊。

ex.s: “Grizzly bears are re-occupying large areas of their former range,” says bear biologist Chris Servheen.
ex.t: “灰熊正在重新占据它们昔日活动范围的大片区域，”熊类生物学家克里斯·瑟夫希恩说。

ex.s: As grizzly bears expand their range into places where they haven’t been seen in a century or more, they’re increasingly being sighted by humans.
ex.t: 随着灰熊的活动范围扩展到它们一个多世纪未见的地方，它们越来越多地被人类看到。

ex.s: The western half of the US was full of grizzlies when Europeans came, with a rough number of 50,000 or more living alongside Native Americans.
ex.t: 当欧洲人到来时，美国西部半壁到处都是灰熊，大约有5万只或更多与美洲原住民比邻而居。

ex.s: In 1975, grizzlies were listed under the Endangered Species Act.
ex.t: 1975年，灰熊被列入《濒危物种法》。

ex.s: Today, there are about 2,000 or more grizzly bears in the US Their recovery has been so successful that the US Fish and Wildlife Service has twice attempted to delist grizzlies, which would loosen legal protections and allow them to be hunted.
ex.t: 如今，美国大约有2000只或更多的灰熊。它们的恢复如此成功，以至于美国鱼类和野生动物管理局曾两次试图将灰熊从保护名录中移除，这将放松法律保护并允许捕猎它们。

ex.s: Both efforts were overturned due to lawsuits from conservation groups.
ex.t: 这两次尝试都因保护组织的诉讼而被推翻。

ex.s: Putting electric fencing around chicken houses and other farm animal quarters is also highly effective at getting grizzlies away.
ex.t: 在鸡舍和其他家畜栏舍周围安装电围栏，对驱赶灰熊也非常有效。

ex.s: They should be kept in national parks.
ex.t: 它们应该被关在国家公园里。

ex.s: They are of high scientific value.
ex.t: 它们有很高的科学价值。

ex.s: They are a symbol of American culture.
ex.t: 它们是美国文化的象征。

ex.t: 从最后一段可以推断出什么？

ex.s: Food should be provided for grizzlies.
ex.t: 应该为灰熊提供食物。

ex.t: 应该为灰熊修建一条专门的通道。

ex.s: Technology can be introduced to protect grizzlies.
ex.t: 可以引入技术来保护灰熊。

ex.s: However, research suggests that if we practiced patience, we’d be a whole lot better off.
ex.t: 然而，研究表明，如果我们练习耐心，我们会好得多。

ex.s: Here are several tricks.

ex.t: 想到讲故事，你脑海中浮现的第一件事，或许是爸妈用各自的嗓音为你讲王子、城堡和怪兽的故事时，你心中形成的幻想世界。

ex.s: We respond to stories, particularly when there is emotional detail.
ex.t: 有其母必有其女。

ex.s: And unlike what we suppose, storytelling is not just a form of entertainment, but a form of learning as well.
ex.t: 而且与我们所想不同，讲故事不仅是一种娱乐形式，也是一种学习形式。

ex.s: Long before reading and writing became widely spread and available, oral storytelling had already been a form that the wisdom and knowledge of the people were passed down from elders to children.
ex.t: 早在读写广泛普及之前，口头讲故事就已是人们将智慧和知识从长辈传给孩子的一种形式。

ex.s: Storytelling helps with learning also because stories are easy to remember.
ex.t: 2023年发表的一项研究旨在探究狗是否能够区分"不愿意"和"不能"给它们食物的人。

ex.s: Research has found that learning obtained from a well-told story is remembered more accurately, and for far longer, than from facts and figures.
ex.t: 研究发现，从一个讲得好的故事中得到的知识，比从事实和数字中得到的记得更准确，也更长久。

ex.s: Stories are an entry point to understanding a different experience of the world.
ex.t: 故事是理解世界不同体验的一个切入点。

ex.s: What are the common elements in all forms of storytelling according to the author?
ex.t: 根据作者的说法，所有讲故事形式中的共同要素是什么？

ex.s: It is more widely available to young learners.
ex.t: 他们假装慢慢走开。

ex.s: It makes what is learned more precise and longer lasting.
ex.t: 他们把香肠拉到狗够不到的地方。

ex.s: Herman Cruse, a school bus driver from New Jersey, has been with Middle Township Public Schools for the past nine years.
ex.t: 赫尔曼·克鲁斯是新泽西州的一名校车司机，过去九年在米德镇公立学校工作。

ex.s: He believes bus drivers are the eyes and ears of students when they're away from home and they have a gift to discern what kids are feeling.
ex.t: 他认为，校车司机是学生们离家时的眼睛和耳朵，并且他们有一种辨别孩子感受的天赋。

ex.s: “Herman is super positive and he's a bright light at our school who makes every child feel loved and heard. ”said Bakley.
ex.t: “赫尔曼特别积极，他是我们学校里的一束光，让每个孩子都感到被爱、被倾听。”巴克利说。

ex.s: It wasn't until he offered to help the boy on the bus that he realized there was something more rewarding he could be doing.
ex.t: 研究发现，从一个讲得好的故事中学到的知识比从事实和数据中学到的记忆更准确、更持久。

ex.s: Why does Cruse think his voluntary work is rewarding according to the last paragraph? (no more than 16 words)
ex.t: 根据最后一段，克鲁斯为什么认为他的志愿工作有意义？（不超过16词）

ex.t: 由于这些原因，它们被誉为"海岸卫士"。

ex.s: So I was shocked when, not long after the email, Professor Mary Devon, who was running the programme, invited me to observe the work being done in her lab.
ex.t: 所以，在那封邮件之后不久，负责该项目的玛丽·德文教授邀请我去观察她的实验室工作时，我感到非常震惊。

ex.s: I jumped at the chance, and a few weeks later I was equally shocked—and overjoyed—when she invited me to talk with her about potential projects I could pursue in her lab.
ex.t: 我立刻抓住机会，几周后，当她邀请我谈谈我可以在她实验室开展的潜在项目时，我同样震惊——且欣喜若狂。

ex.s: What she proposed didn’t seem as exciting as the original project I had applied to, but I was going to give it my all.
ex.t: 她提出的方案看起来不如我最初申请的那个项目令人兴奋，但我决定全力以赴。

ex.t: 当我被一个看似完美契合的职位拒绝时，无疑很难受。

ex.s: It helped that in the end I was accepted into one of the other programmes I was also excited about.
ex.t: 好在最后我被另一个我也同样期待的项目录取了。

ex.s: In recent years, researchers from diverse fields have agreed that short-termism is now a significant problem in industrialised societies.
ex.t: 近年来，来自不同领域的研究者一致认为，短视主义如今在工业化社会是一个重要问题。

ex.s: These biased perspectives cannot be blamed on one single cause.
ex.t: 这些有偏见的观点不能归因于任何一个单一原因。

ex.s: It is fair to say, though, that our psychological biases play a major role.
ex.t: 不过，公平地说，我们的心理偏见起着主要作用。

ex.s: People’s hesitancy to delay satisfaction is the most obvious example, but there are others.
ex.t: 人们不愿意延迟满足是最明显的例子，但还有其他例子。

ex.s: One of them is about how the most accessible information in the present affects decisions about the future.
ex.t: 其中一个是关于：当下最容易获取的信息如何影响对未来的决定。

ex.s: This is when a pop star draws far more attention than, say, gradual biodiversity decline.
ex.t: 这就是当一位流行明星比，比如说，渐进的生物多样性衰退吸引更多关注时的情况。

ex.s: Indeed, when it comes to environmental transformations, we can develop a form of collective “poor memory”, and each new generation can believe the state of affairs they encounter is nothing out of the ordinary.
ex.t: 的确，在环境变化方面，我们会产生一种集体的"健忘"，每一代新人都可能认为他们所遇到的事态再正常不过。

ex.s: What can be inferred from the last paragraph?
ex.t: 从最后一段可以推断出什么？

ex.s: Climate change has been forgotten.
ex.t: 气候变化已经被遗忘。

ex.s: Lessons of history are highly valued.
ex.t: 历史的教训受到高度重视。

ex.s: The human mind is bad at noting slow change.
ex.t: 人类大脑不善于察觉缓慢的变化。

ex.s: Humans are unwilling to admit their shortcomings.
ex.t: 人类不愿承认自己的缺点。

ex.s: What is life?
ex.t: 什么是生命？

ex.s: Like most great questions, this one is easy to ask but difficult to answer.
ex.t: 像大多数重大问题一样，这个问题容易提出却难以回答。

ex.s: The reason is simple: we know of just one type of life and it’s challenging to do science with a sample size of one.
ex.t: 原因很简单：我们只知道一种生命，而用样本量为一来做科学是很有挑战性的。

ex.s: The field of artificial life-called ALife for short — is the systematic attempt to spell out life’s fundamental principles.
ex.t: 人工生命领域——简称ALife——是系统性地阐明生命基本原理的尝试。

ex.s: Many of these practitioners, so-called ALifers, think that somehow making life is the surest way to really understand what life is.
ex.t: 这些从业者中的许多——所谓的ALife研究者——认为，以某种方式创造生命是真正理解生命的最佳途径。

ex.s: Alan Smith, a complexity scientist, is tired of such complaints.
ex.t: 复杂性科学家艾伦·史密斯厌倦了这类抱怨。

ex.s: Asking about “the point” of ALife might be, well, missing the point entirely, he says.
ex.t: 他说，问人工生命（ALife）的“意义”是什么，可能恰恰完全没问到点子上。

ex.s: “The existence of a living system is not about the use of anything.” Alan says.
ex.t: 生命系统的存在并不关乎对任何东西的利用，艾伦说。

ex.s: “Some people ask me, ‘So what’s the worth of artificial life?’ Do you ever think, ‘What is the worth of your grandmother?’”
ex.t: "有人问我，'那人工生命有什么价值？'你有没有想过，'你祖母的价值是什么？'"

ex.s: This is the capacity for a system to create essentially endless complexity, to be a sort of “novelty generator”.
ex.t: 这是一种系统创造近乎无限复杂性的能力，成为某种"新颖性生成器"。

ex.s: The only system known to exhibit this is Earth’s biosphere.
ex.t: 已知唯一能展示这种能力的系统是地球的生物圈。

ex.s: Compared with the developments of Al, advances in ALife are harder to recognize.
ex.t: 与人工智能的发展相比，ALife的进展更难被识别。

ex.s: One reason is that ALife is a field in which the central concept — life itself — is undefined.
ex.t: 一个原因是，ALife是一个核心概念——生命本身——尚未被定义的研究领域。

ex.s: The result is a diverse line of projects that each advance along their unique paths.
ex.t: 其结果是一系列多元的项目，各自沿着独特的路径推进。

ex.s: It may be, of course, that these characteristics aren’t in any way surprising or singular.
ex.t: 当然，这些特征可能在任何方面都不令人惊讶或独特。

ex.s: Ultimately ALife may be nothing special.
ex.t: 最终，ALife可能并没有什么特别之处。

ex.s: Regarding Alan Smith’s defence of ALife, the author is      .
ex.t: 关于艾伦·史密斯对ALife的辩护，作者持      态度。

ex.s: When I talk to families as a scholar of higher education, they’re often surprised that teaching excellence is not counted in rankings. ____36____
ex.t: 当我以高等教育学者的身份与家庭交谈时，他们常常惊讶于教学卓越并未被计入排名。____36____

ex.s: Emerging research suggests that courses in lower-ranked universities, on average, scored higher on teaching than courses in higher-ranked universities. ____37____ The absence of teaching excellence from the rankings is surprising given the link between high-quality teaching and student success.
ex.t: 新兴研究表明，平均而言，排名较低大学的课程在教学方面的得分高于排名较高的大学。____37____ 考虑到高质量教学与学生成功之间的联系，排名中缺少教学质量这一点令人惊讶。

ex.s: Rankings, however, are only one reason why a low value is placed on teaching in higher education.
ex.t: 然而，排名只是高等教育中教学价值被低估的一个原因。

ex.s: What is the result?
ex.t: 结果是什么？

ex.s: They should give strong consideration to universities where high-quality teaching is valued, even though the schools may be ranked lower.
ex.t: 他们应该认真考虑那些重视高质量教学的大学，即使这些学校的排名较低。

ex.s: They’re even more surprised at how teaching is undervalued by universities.
ex.t: 他们甚至更惊讶于大学如何低估教学。

ex.s: Habit formation is the process by which behaviours become automatic.
ex.t: 习惯养成是行为变得自动化的过程。

ex.s: People develop countless habits as they explore the world, whether they are aware of them or not.
ex.t: 人们在探索世界的过程中养成无数的习惯，无论他们是否意识到这一点。

ex.s: Understanding how habits take shape may be helpful in changing bad habits.
ex.t: 了解习惯如何形成可能有助于改变坏习惯。

ex.s: Habits are built through learning and repetition.
ex.t: 习惯是通过学习和重复建立的。

ex.s: A “habit loop(环)” is a way of describing several related elements that produce habits.
ex.t: "习惯环"是描述产生习惯的几个相关要素的一种方式。

ex.s: These elements are called the cue, the routine, and the reward.
ex.t: 这些要素被称为提示、常规和奖励。

ex.s: While a routine involves repeated behaviour, it’s not necessarily performed in response to a deep﹣rooted urge, as a habit is.
ex.t: 虽然常规包含重复行为，但它未必像习惯那样是出于根深蒂固的冲动而做出的。

ex.s: Old habits can be difficult to shake, and healthy habits are often harder to develop.
ex.t: 旧习惯可能很难改掉，而健康习惯往往更难养成。

ex.s: While you are able to pickup a new habit in a few weeks, it takes many months to build a healthy habit.
ex.t: 虽然你可以在几周内养成一个新习惯，但建立一个健康习惯需要好几个月。

ex.t: 习惯是如何养成的？

ex.s: In what way is a routine different from a habit?
ex.t: 常规与习惯在哪些方面不同？

ex.s: Like most of us, I try to be mindful of food that goes to waste.
ex.t: 像大多数人一样，我尽量注意不要浪费食物。

ex.s: It’s jaw-dropping how much perfectly good food is thrown away — from “ugly” (but quite eatable) vegetables rejected by grocers to large amounts of uneaten dishes thrown into restaurant garbage cans.
ex.t: 完美完好的食物被扔掉的数量令人震惊——从杂货商拒绝的"丑陋"（但完全可以食用）的蔬菜到大量被扔进餐厅垃圾桶的剩菜。

ex.s: In fact, Royte writes, “if food waste were a country, it would be the third largest producer of greenhouse gases in the world.”
ex.t: 事实上，罗伊特写道："如果食物浪费是一个国家，它将是世界第三大温室气体排放国。"

ex.s: Curtin is CEO of DC Central Kitchen in Washington, D.C., which recovers food and turns it into healthy meals.
ex.t: Curtin是华盛顿特区DC Central Kitchen的首席执行官，该公司回收食物并将其转化为健康餐食。

ex.s: Buy only what is needed.

ex.s: But why are certain sounds more common than others?
ex.t: 但为什么某些声音比其他声音更常见呢？

ex.s: A ground-breaking, five-year study shows that diet-related changes in human bite led to new speech sounds that are now found in half the world’s languages.
ex.t: 一项开创性的五年研究表明，与人类咬合相关的饮食变化导致了新的语音，如今这些语音存在于世界上一半的语言中。

ex.s: More than 30 years ago, the scholar Charles Hockett noted that speech sounds called labiodentals, such as “f” and “v”, were more common in the languages of societies that ate softer foods.
ex.t: 30多年前，学者Charles Hockett注意到，被称为唇齿音的语音（如"f"和"v"）在饮食较软的社会的语言中更为常见。

ex.s: The team showed that this change in bite was connected with the development of agriculture in the Neolithic period.
ex.t: 团队表明，这种咬合变化与新石器时代农业的发展有关。

ex.s: The jawbone didn’t have to do as much work and so didn’t grow to be so large.
ex.t: 颌骨不必那么用力，所以长得没那么大了。

ex.s: Analyses of a language database also confirmed that there was a global change in the sound of world languages after the Neolithic age, with the use of “f” and “v” increasing remarkably during the last few thousand years.
ex.t: 对一个语言数据库的分析也证实，新石器时代之后世界语言的声音发生了全球性的变化，"f"和"v"的使用在近几千年显著增加。

ex.s: These sounds are still not found in the languages of many hunter-gatherer people today.
ex.t: 这些声音在今天许多狩猎采集民族的语言中仍然不存在。

ex.s: This research overturns the popular view that all human speech sounds were present when human beings evolved around 300,000 years ago. ”The set of speech sounds we use has not necessarily remained stable since the appearance of human beings, but rather the huge variety of speech sounds that we find today is the product of a complex interplay of things like biological change and cultural evolution,“ said Steven Moran, a member of the research team.
ex.t: 这项研究推翻了“人类约30万年前进化时所有语音都已存在”的流行观点。“我们使用的语音集合自人类出现以来未必保持稳定，我们今天发现的极其多样的语音，是生物变化和文化演变等事物复杂相互作用的产物，”研究团队成员史蒂文·莫兰说。

ex.s: Over the last seven years, most states have banned texting by drivers, and public service campaigns have tried a wide range of methods to persuade people to put down their phones when they are behind the wheel.
ex.t: 过去七年里，大多数州已禁止司机发短信，公益宣传用了多种方法说服人们开车时放下手机。

ex.s: Yet the problem, by just about any measure, appears to be getting worse.
ex.t: 然而，无论从哪个标准看，这个问题似乎都在变得更糟。

ex.s: Americans are still texting while driving, as well as using social networks and taking photos.
ex.t: 美国人仍在开车时发短信，同时使用社交网络和拍照。

ex.s: Road accidents, which had fallen for years, are now rising sharply.
ex.t: 多年来下降的交通事故，现在正急剧上升。

ex.s: So to try to change a distinctly modern behavior, lawmakers and public health experts are reaching back to an old approach: They want to treat distracted driving like drunk driving.
ex.t: 所以，为了改变一种明显的现代行为，立法者和公共卫生专家正回溯到一种老办法：他们想把分心驾驶当作酒驾来对待。

ex.s: An idea from lawmakers in New York is to give police officers a new device called the Textalyzer.
ex.t: 纽约立法者提出一个想法，给警察一种名为Textalyzer的新设备。

ex.s: The technology could determine whether a driver had just texted, emailed or done anything else that is not allowed under New York's hands-free driving laws.
ex.t: 该技术能判断司机是否刚刚发过短信、邮件或做了纽约免提驾驶法所不允许的其他事情。

ex.s: If the Textalyzer bill becomes law, he said, "people are going to be more afraid to put their hands on the cell phone."

ex.s: As we age, even if we're healthy, the heart just isn't as efficient in processing oxygen as it used to be.
ex.t: 大多数人在50多岁或60岁出头时首先出现迹象。

ex.s: In the beginning, it is flexible, but put it in a drawer for 20 years and it will become dry and easily broken," says Dr Ben Levine, a heart specialist at the University of Texas.
ex.t: 起初它是有弹性的，但把它放在抽屉里20年，它就会变干、易断，得克萨斯大学的心脏专家本·莱文博士说。

ex.s: Fortunately for those in midlife, Levine is finding that even if you haven't been an enthusiastic exerciser, getting in shape now may help improve your aging heart.
ex.t: 对那些中年人来说幸运的是，莱文发现，即使你一直不是热衷锻炼的人，现在开始健身也可能有助于改善你衰老的心脏。

ex.s: Levine and his research team selected volunteers aged between 45 and 64 who did not exercise much but were otherwise healthy.
ex.t: Levine和他的研究团队选择了45至64岁之间不常运动但其他方面健康的志愿者。

ex.s: Participants were randomly divided into two groups.
ex.t: 参与者被随机分成两组。

ex.s: "The sweet spot in life to start exercising, if you haven't already, is in late middle age when the heart still has flexibility," Levine says.
ex.t: "如果你还没有开始运动，生命中开始运动的最佳时期是中年晚期，这时心脏仍有弹性，"Levine说。

ex.s: Dr Nieca Goldberg, a spokeswoman for the American Heart Association, says Levine's findings are a great start.
ex.t: 美国心脏协会发言人涅卡·戈德堡博士说，莱文的发现是一个很好的开端。

ex.s: But the study was small and needs to be repeated with far larger groups of people to determine exactly which aspects of an exercise routine make the biggest difference.
ex.t: 但这项研究规模小，需要用大得多的人群重复，以确切确定锻炼计划的哪些方面影响最大。

ex.s: In which aspect were the two groups different in terms of research design?
ex.t: 两组在研究设计上有什么不同？

ex.s: High-intensity exercise is more suitable for the young.
ex.t: 高强度运动更适合年轻人。

ex.s: It is never too late for people to start taking exercise.
ex.t: 开始运动永远不嫌晚。

ex.s: Writing an essay is a difficult process for most people.

ex.t: 然而，如果你学会练习三种简单技巧，这个过程可以变得更容易。

ex.s: 36   When you are first trying to think of ideas for an essay, put your pen to your paper and write nonstop for ten or fifteen minutes without letting your pen leave the paper.
ex.t: 36 当你最初试图为论文想点子时，把笔放在纸上，连续写十到十五分钟，不让笔离开纸。

ex.s: The next technique is to write your draft rapidly without worrying about being perfect.
ex.t: 下一个技巧是快速写草稿，不必担心完美。

ex.s: After you have revised your draft until it is too messy to work from anymore, you can enter your changes into your word processor.
ex.t: 当你修订草稿直到乱得无法再用时，可以把改动输入文字处理软件。

ex.s: Make sure your handwriting is neat.

ex.s: The second draft of the essay should be better.
ex.t: 作文的第二稿应该更好。

ex.s: Goffin’s cockatoos, a kind of small parrot native to Australasia, have been shown to have similar shape-recognition abilities to a human two-year-old.
ex.t: 戈芬氏凤头鹦鹉是一种原产于澳大拉西亚的小鹦鹉，已被证明具有与人类两岁幼儿相似的形状识别能力。

ex.s: In a recent experiment, cockatoos were presented with a box with a nut inside it.
ex.t: 在最近一项实验中，凤头鹦鹉面对一个里面装着坚果的盒子。

ex.s: The clear front of the box had a “keyhole” in a geometric shape, and the birds were given five differently shaped “keys” to choose from.
ex.t: 盒子的透明正面有一个几何形状的"钥匙孔"，鸟儿有五把不同形状的"钥匙"可供选择。

ex.s: This ability to recognize that a shape will need to be turned in a specific direction before it will fit is called an “allocentric frame of reference”.
ex.t: 这种认识到形状需要朝特定方向旋转才能契合的能力，被称为"allocentric frame of reference"（客体参照框架）。

ex.s: In the experiment, Goffin’s cockatoos were able to select the right tool for the job, in most cases, by visual recognition alone.
ex.t: 在实验中，戈芬氏凤头鹦鹉在大多数情况下仅凭视觉识别就能为任务选对工具。

ex.s: Where trial-and-error was used, the cockatoos did better than monkeys in similar tests.
ex.t: 在使用试错法的情况下，凤头鹦鹉的表现优于类似测试中的猴子。

ex.s: How far they are able to see.
ex.t: 他们能看多远。

ex.s: Whether they are smarter than monkeys.
ex.t: 它们是否比猴子聪明。

ex.s: A few years later, as I stood in the lunch line with my kindergarten class in a school in Brooklyn, I realized things were no longer that simple.
ex.t: 几年后，当我和幼儿园班级在布鲁克林一所学校排队吃午餐时，我意识到事情不再那么简单。

ex.s: The food choices were almost as diverse as the students.
ex.t: 食物选择几乎和学生一样多样化。

ex.s: In front of me was an array of foods I couldn’t even name in my native language.
ex.t: 我面前是一排我甚至无法用母语叫出名字的食物。

ex.s: I often had to be an interpreter for the Italian-speaking ones.
ex.t: 我常常得给说意大利语的人当口译。

ex.s: As I served the role of vital communication link, I was reminded of my desperate struggle to converse before I learned English.
ex.t: 当我担任重要沟通纽带的角色时，我想起了我在学会英语之前那种拼命想交流的挣扎。

ex.s: It suddenly became very clear to me how lucky I was to be fluent in two languages.
ex.t: 我突然非常清楚地意识到我能流利地说两种语言是多么幸运。

ex.s: In New York, a multicultural city, students like me are blessed with a chance to work with a diverse population.
ex.t: 在纽约这样一个多元文化的城市，像我这样的学生有幸能与多样化的人群一起工作。

ex.t: 这份工作在课堂四壁之内不可能实现的方式上拓展了我的心胸。

ex.s: Walking through the streets of Brooklyn today, I am no longer confused by this city’s sounds and smells.
ex.t: 今天走在布鲁克林的街道上，我不再对这个城市的声音和气味感到困惑。

ex.t: 这就是微型森林运动，旨在证明生活中最好的东西确实来自小包装。

ex.s: “We focus on urban areas where access to nature is often not that easy”, says Hartley.

ex.t: 小森林里的树有什么特别之处？

ex.s: They are small in size.

ex.s: High conscientiousness is related to lower job performance, especially in simple jobs where it doesn’t pay to be a perfectionist.

ex.s: The young banker who eats lunch at his desk is probably seen as a go-getter, while his colleagues who chat over a relaxed conference-room meal get dirty looks from the corner office.
ex.t: 在办公桌前吃午餐的年轻银行家可能被视为积极进取的人，而那些在轻松的会议室用餐闲聊的同事，却会招来角落办公室（高管）的白眼。

ex.t: 来自比我们更看重关系的文化的人们，一想到在电脑前独自吃饭就会震惊，得克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校心理学教授阿特·马克曼说。

ex.s: “Also, there is a lot of research showing that a positive mood leads to higher levels of productivity and creativity.

ex.t: 最好的沟通者是那些知道如何根据读者调整语言的人。

ex.t: 但它总是有目的的——至少应该是这样。

ex.t: 你写"亲爱的爷爷奶奶"是因为你们关系亲密。

ex.s: I thought that we would just be passing out dinners to those in need, but I found out we would be doing everything from preparing to serving the dinner.
ex.t: 我以为我们只是分发晚餐给那些需要帮助的人，但我发现我们要做的事情从准备到服务晚餐无所不包。

ex.s: Much still needed to be done before dinner was served, but already outside the building many homeless people were gathering.
ex.t: 晚餐供应之前还有很多事情要做，但建筑物外面已经聚集了许多无家可归的人。

ex.s: She smiled at me and said if I needed help, she’d be right there, which I found quite comforting.
ex.t: 她对我微笑说如果需要帮助她就在那里，我觉得这很令人安慰。

ex.s: They were of all ages and nationalities.
ex.t: 他们有各种年龄和国籍。

ex.t: 大多数人穿着破旧脏污的衣服。

ex.t: 我很高兴能以这种方式获得服务时长。

ex.t: 一个周一早晨，当孩子们正享受自由玩耍时，我走到教室门口休息一下。

ex.t: 这正是那扇我____2____引导孩子们穿过以确保他们免受严寒侵袭的门。

ex.t: 他一定在那儿等了很久了！

ex.t: 他的手被治疗冻伤。

ex.t: 第二天早上，最先____6____到达的之一就是那个冻伤了的小男孩。

ex.t: 他不仅精力充沛地跑进来，而且他的____7____声音像往常一样响亮！

ex.t: 我给了他一个温暖的拥抱，告诉他见到他我是多么（第8空）。

ex.t: 一种理论，越来越多地____14____  (support)得到专家支持，认为气味偏好是后天习得的。

ex.t: 这已被采用以确保更容易检测燃气泄漏。

ex.s: However, a strong smell is added so that we can raise the alarm when we detect the smell associated with danger.
ex.t: 然而，会加入一种强烈的气味，这样当我们察觉到与危险相关的气味时就能发出警报。

ex.t: 我的完美主义倾向是主要原因：我想在所做的任何事情上都做到完美，这在生活中显然是不可能的，但它吞噬了我。

ex.s: This first contact was where my story began.
ex.t: 第一次接触就是我的故事的开始。

ex.s: Looking back, I now see that this would be the first in a series of timely opportunities that my old self would have let pass, but that this new and more confident Alice enthusiastically seized.
ex.t: 回首过去，我现在明白，这将是一系列及时机会中的第一个——过去的我会让它们溜走，但这个更自信的新艾丽斯热情地抓住了。

ex.s: Shortly after I received his invitation, applications to join the Youth for Nature and the Youth for Planet groups were sent around through my high school.
ex.t: 我收到他的邀请后不久，加入“青年与自然”和“青年与地球”小组的申请表就在我的高中传开了。

ex.s: It was that voice in the back of my head telling me that one phrase that has stopped so many people from reaching their potential: I can’t.
ex.t: 正是我脑海中的那个声音告诉我那个阻止许多人发挥潜力的短语：我不行。

ex.s: They say good things come to those who wait; I say: grab every opportunity with everything you have and be impatient.
ex.t: 人们说好事多磨；我说：用你拥有的一切抓住每一个机会，要有紧迫感。

ex.t: Alice焦虑的主要原因是什么？

ex.t: 这种技能教授给艺术家和工程师，但很少教授给科学家。

ex.t: 结果——一种被称为系统思维的方法——现在被视为应对全球挑战的关键。

ex.t: 但一些科学家利用机器学习和人工智能提出，人类饮食至少包含26000种生化物质——且绝大多数不为人知。这表明，在达成系统思维的第一个目标之前我们还有路要走——在这个例子中，就是识别营养系统中更多的组成部分。

ex.s: A friend has been sending me articles on how quantum computers might help solve some of the biggest challenges we face as humans.
ex.t: 一位朋友一直给我发文章，讲量子计算机如何帮助解决人类面临的一些最大挑战。

ex.s: One is computer scientist Chris Johnson who I see as someone who helps keep the field honest The other is physicist Philip Taylor.
ex.t: 一位是计算机科学家Chris Johnson，我认为他是一个有助于保持该领域诚实的人。另一位是物理学家Philip Taylor。

ex.s: For decades, quantum computing has been little more than a laboratory curiosity.
ex.t: 几十年来，量子计算不过是一种实验室里的新奇事物。

ex.s: He worries that researchers are making promises they can’t keep.
ex.t: 他担心研究人员做出了他们无法兑现的承诺。

ex.s: “What’s new,” Johnson wrote, “is that millions of dollars are now potentially available to quantum computing researchers.”
ex.t: "新的变化是，"Johnson写道，"现在可能有数百万美元可用于量子计算研究人员。"

ex.s: But something about quantum computing makes it especially prone to hype, Johnson suggests, perhaps because “‘quantum’ stands for something cool you shouldn’t be able to understand.” And that brings me back to Taylor, who suggested that I read his book Q for Quantum.
ex.t: 但约翰逊认为，量子计算的某些特质让它尤其容易炒作，也许是因为“‘量子’代表着某种你本不该能理解的酷东西”。这让我又想到泰勒，他建议我读他的书《量子Q》。

ex.s: Some scientists insist that once we discover the truth about the world, we are done.

ex.s: In science, what we do is both hard and, often, hard to explain.
ex.t: 在科学领域，我们所做的既困难，而且往往也难以解释。

ex.s: Science is a process of learning and discovery, and sometimes we learn that what we thought was right is wrong.
ex.t: 科学是一个学习和发现的过程，有时我们学到，我们原以为对的东西是错的。

ex.s: The concept of beauty today is very different from what it was in ancient Greece or the Middle Ages, and so are most of our “laws” of nature.
ex.t: 如今美的概念与古希腊或中世纪时的概念大不相同，我们大多数自然"定律"也是如此。

ex.s: Other scientists may say scientific findings are true because they use “the scientific method.” But we can never actually agree on what that method is.
ex.t: 其他科学家可能说科学发现是真的，因为他们用了“科学方法”。但我们永远无法真正就那方法是什么达成一致。

ex.s: Some will say it is observation and description of the world.
ex.t: 有人说它是对世界的观察和描述。

ex.s: Others will say it is the use of experience and experiment.
ex.t: 也有人说它是经验和实验的运用。

ex.s: Recently a leading scientist said the scientific method was to avoid fooling oneself into thinking something is true that is not.
ex.t: 最近，一位顶尖科学家说，科学方法就是避免自欺欺人地相信不真实的东西。

ex.s: Each of these views has its value, but if the claim is that any one of these is the scientific method, then they all fail.
ex.t: 这些观点各有价值，但如果声称其中任何一个是唯一的科学方法，那么它们都不成立。

ex.s: Scientists have bitterly argued about which methods are the best, and, as we all know, bitter arguments rarely get resolved.
ex.t: 科学家们激烈地争论哪些方法最好，而众所周知，激烈的争论很少能解决。

ex.s: In my view, science is not simple, and neither is the natural world.
ex.t: 在我看来，科学并不简单，自然界也不简单。

ex.s: Our efforts to understand and explain the natural world are just that: efforts.
ex.t: 我们理解和解释自然界的努力仅仅是努力而已。

ex.s: The good news is that when that happens, we pick ourselves up, brush ourselves off, and get back to work.
ex.t: 好消息是，当失败发生时，我们会重新站起来，拍掉身上的灰尘，继续工作。

ex.s: Understanding the world we live in, and using that knowledge to do useful things, is its own reward.
ex.t: 理解我们所生活的世界，并用这些知识做有用的事，本身就是一种回报。

ex.s: Many people now misunderstand emotional intelligence as almost everything desirable in a person's makeup that cannot be measured by an IQ test, such as character, motivation, confidence, mental stability, optimism and "people skills." Research has shown that emotional skills may contribute to some of these qualities, but most of them move far beyond skill-based emotional intelligence.
ex.t: 现在许多人把情商误解为一个人特质中几乎所有无法用智商测试衡量的可取之处，比如性格、动力、自信、心理稳定、乐观和“人际技巧”。研究表明，情绪技能可能有助于其中一些品质，但大多数远远超出了基于技能的情商。

ex.s: We prefer to describe emotional intelligence as a specific set of skills that can be used for either good or bad purposes.
ex.t: 我们倾向于把情商描述为一组特定的技能，可以用于好的或坏的目的。

ex.s: The ability to accurately understand how others are feeling may be used by a doctor to find how best to help her patients, while a cheater might use it to control potential victims.
ex.t: 准确理解他人感受的能力，医生可以用来找到最好地帮助病人的方法，而骗子可能用它来控制潜在受害者。

ex.s: Being emotionally intelligent does not necessarily make one a moral person.

ex.s: Leslie Nielsen’s childhood was a difficult one, but he had one particular shining star in his life — his uncle, who was a well-known actor.
ex.t: 莱斯利·尼尔森的童年很艰难，但他生命中有一颗特别闪亮的星——他的叔叔，一位知名演员。

ex.s: Even though he often felt he would be discovered to be a no-talent, he moved forward, gaining a scholarship to the Neighborhood Playhouse and making his first television appearance a few years later in 1948.
ex.t: 尽管他常常觉得自己会被发现毫无才华，他仍继续前行，获得了邻里剧院的奖学金，并在几年后的1948年首次登上电视。

ex.s: Nielsen always felt he should be doing comedy but his good looks and distinguished voice kept him busy in dramatic roles.

ex.s: He was thrilled to be doing the comedy that he always felt he should do, but even during his last few years, he always had a sense of curiosity, wondering what new role or challenge might be just around the corner.

ex.s: He realised that something needed to change, and, being a London media type, appointed himself "marketing director for Nature".

ex.s: He documented his journey as he set about treating nature as a brand to be marketed to young people.

ex.s: The result was Project Wild Thing, a film which charts the birth of the Wild Network a group of organisations with the common goal of getting children out into nature.
ex.t: 成果是《野生动物计划》这部影片，它记录了“野生网络”的诞生——一个由多个组织组成的、以让孩子走进自然为共同目标的团体。

ex.s: "There is a lot of really interesting evidence which seems to be suggesting that if children are inspired up to the age of seven, then being outdoors will be a habit for life." His own children have got into the habit of playing outside now: "We just send them out into the garden and tell them not to come back in for a while."

ex.s: If you ever get the impression that your dog can "tell" whether you look content or annoyed, you may be onto something.

ex.s: Dogs may indeed be able to distinguish between happy and angry human faces, according to a new study.
ex.t: 一项新研究表明，狗确实能够区分人类高兴和生气的面孔。

ex.s: During the training stage, each dog was shown only the upper half or the lower half of the person’s face.
ex.t: 研究人员发现狗能够通过用鼻子触摸图片来选择生气或开心的脸而且频率高于随机概率。

ex.s: The researchers found that the dogs were able to pick the angry or happy face by touching a picture of it with their noses more often than one would expect by random chance.
ex.t: 研究人员发现，狗用鼻子触碰开心或生气面孔图片的频率，高于随机概率下的预期。

ex.s: At this point, it is not clear why dogs seem to be equipped with the ability to recognize different facial expressions in humans.

ex.t: 你不必成为群体中的笑话王才能展示你的幽默感。

ex.s: You can be the one who directs the conversation to fun topics that are ripe for others to add humor.
ex.t: 你可以引导对话到有趣的话题，让别人容易加入幽默。

ex.s: When people see you trying to be funny, it frees them to try it themselves.
ex.t: 当人们看到你在努力变得有趣时，这让他们也敢于尝试。

ex.t: 所以即使你自己的幽默努力不够完美，你也可能释放了他人心中长期压抑的幽默。

ex.s: People need permission to be funny in social settings because there’s always a risk that comes with humor.
ex.t: 在社交场合，人们需要被允许才能表现风趣，因为幽默总伴随着风险。

ex.s: Some people--and I was one of them--believe that humorous complaints about the little problems of life make humor, and sometimes that is the case.

ex.s: You have to be at least a bit self-assured to laugh at yourself in front of others.

ex.s: I always wanted to know what my mom was reading． Hearing mom say，"I can't believe what's printed in the newspaper this morning，" made me want to grab it out of her hands and read it myself． I wanted to be like my mom and know all of the things she knew． So I carried around a book， and each night， just to be like her， I would pretend to be reading．
ex.t: 我一直想知道妈妈在读什么。听到妈妈说“我真不敢相信今天早上报纸上印了什么”，让我想从她手里抢过来自己读。我想像妈妈一样，知道她知道的所有事情。所以我随身带一本书，每天晚上，只是为了像她，我会假装在读书。

ex.s: This is how everyone learned to read． We would start off with sentences， then paragraphs， and then stories． It seemed an unending journey， but even as a six﹣year﹣old girl I realized that knowing how to read could open many doors． When mom said， "The C﹣A﹣N﹣D﹣Y is hidden on the top shelf，" I knew where the candy was． My progress in reading raised my curiosity， and I wanted to know everything． I often found myself telling my mom to drive more slowly， so that I could read all of the road signs we passed．
ex.t: 这就是每个人学习阅读的方式。我们从句子开始，再到段落，然后是故事。这似乎是一段无尽的旅程，但即便作为六岁女孩，我也意识到会阅读能打开许多扇门。当妈妈说“C-A-N-D-Y藏在顶层架子上”时，我知道糖在哪里。我在阅读上的进步激发了好奇心，我想知道一切。我常发现自己让妈妈开慢些，好让我能读完我们经过的所有路标。

ex.s: Most of my reading through primary， middle and high school was factual reading． I read for knowledge， and to make A's on my tests． Occasionally， I would read a novel that was assigned， but I didn't enjoy this type of reading． I liked facts， things that are concrete． I thought anything abstract left too much room for argument．
ex.t: 我小学、初中和高中的阅读大多是事实性阅读。我为获取知识而读，也为考试拿A而读。偶尔我会读被布置的小说，但我不喜欢这类阅读。我喜欢事实、具体的事物。我觉得任何抽象的东西都留给争论太多空间。

ex.s: Yet， now that I'm growing and the world I once knew as being so simple is becoming more complex， I find myself needing a way to escape． By opening a novel， I can leave behind my burdens and enter into a wonderful and mysterious world where I am now a new character． In these worlds I can become anyone． I don't have to write down what happened or what technique the author was using when he or she wrote this． I just read to relax．
ex.t: 然而，如今我在成长，曾经以为简单的世界变得复杂，我发现自己需要一种逃避的方式。打开一本小说，我就能放下重担，进入一个奇妙而神秘的世界，在那里我成了新角色。在这些世界里我可以是任何人的。我不必记下发生了什么，或作者写作时用了什么技巧。我读只是为了放松。

ex.s: And unplanned human activities have proved the idea of top﹣down control by top predators to be true． In the ocean， we fished for top predators such as cod on an industrial scale， while on land， we killed off large predators such as wolves． These actions have greatly affected the ecological balance．

ex.s: When I was a little girl， my family moved to a tiny town at the bottom of a big mountain． One day after school， while exploring the green woods of this magnificent mountain， I almost fell on a set of stairs． What could these steps lead to？ Curiosity got the best of me as I knew it would be starting to get dark soon． I started climbing up those strangely mysterious steps．
ex.t: 我小时候，全家搬到大山脚下的一座小镇。一天放学后，在探索这座雄伟青山的绿林时，我差点绊倒在一组台阶上。这些台阶通向何处？好奇心占了上风，因为我知道天快黑了。我开始爬上那些神秘怪异的台阶。

ex.s: I climbed and climbed． There was nothing but just green bushes and these steps． I had to reach the top!
ex.t: 现在我们生活在一个充满"做不到"的态度的世界里。我们都会跌倒。我们都有疑虑和遗憾。但我们仍然必须攀登，梦想着我们山顶上有什么。怪物可能会出现，或者黑夜将会降临。但永远不要放弃你的梦想！

ex.s: But it was now getting real dark． If I kept going I might not be able to see my way back． My mum would be worried sick if I didn't come home soon． So I ran back home almost in the dark while trying not to get too scared．
